title: Joining a Gym for the First Time in NZ — What to Expect and How to Choose
meta_desc: Joining a gym in NZ? Learn what to expect, how to choose and compare prices from $10/week
intro: Joining a gym for the first time can be daunting, but with the right information, you can make an informed decision. In NZ, the average gym membership costs around $30-40 per week. With numerous options available, it's essential to consider factors like contract terms, facilities, and prices before making a commitment.

sections.heading: What to Look for in a Gym
sections.body: When choosing a gym, consider factors like location, operating hours, equipment, group classes, and personal training options. Look for gyms with a supportive environment, clean facilities, and a variety of membership options. Some popular gym franchises in NZ include Anytime Fitness, Snap Fitness, and CityFitness.

sections.heading: Trial Passes and Induction Sessions
sections.body: Many gyms offer trial passes or guest passes, allowing you to try out their facilities before committing to a membership. Take advantage of these offers to get a feel for the gym's atmosphere and equipment. Induction sessions are also a great way to learn about the gym's facilities and get a personalized workout plan.

sections.heading: Contract Terms and Pricing
sections.body: Be wary of contracts that lock you in for extended periods. Some gyms offer flexible membership options with no fixed-term contracts, while others may require a 12-month commitment. sections.heading: Best Starter Gyms in NZ
sections.body: If you're new to gyms, consider starting with a more affordable option. Some great starter gyms in NZ include Jetts Fitness, which offers a $10 per week membership with no contract, and Snap Fitness, which has a $19.95 per week membership option with a 6-month contract.

sections.heading: Making the Most of Your Gym Membership
sections.body: To get the most out of your gym membership, create a workout routine, set achievable goals, and track your progress. Don't be afraid to ask for help from gym staff or personal trainers, and take advantage of group classes and other amenities like pools and saunas.
